title: The Dollar Breakout is Starting
speaker: A1 Trading hosts (incl. Marco)

macro_themes.view: The Fed rarely hikes once; with CPI forecast 3.6% vs 3.4% prior and PCE trending higher, another hike is expected.

macro_themes.theme: Small caps hurt by higher rates
macro_themes.view: Indebted, often unprofitable small caps suffer most from rising yields and floating-rate debt.
Strong GDP and ADP outweigh a cooler PCE print; net outcome bearish for metals and supportive of the dollar.
A few large companies hold up Nasdaq and SPY while most stocks fall.

macro_themes.theme: Middle East / oil keeps inflation elevated
macro_themes.view: Elevated oil keeps inflation up; a resolution would let the Russell play catch-up.

calls.condition: Second host wants the support level and the 200-day SMA to break; an end to the Iran/oil situation would be the bullish risk (Russell catches up).
calls.reason: Backtest of 5 Fed hiking cycles since 1987 shows Russell falls a median 6-8% over following weeks; small caps most debt-exposed; Edge Finder bearish.
calls.quote: I'm thinking the Russell could drop from here to maybe like 2,600, something like that.

calls.reason: Strong GDP, strong ADP and a hawkish Fed are 'strong dollar fundamental data points'; a cooler PCE is the only offsetting factor.
calls.quote: You had this case where you have a lots of a lot of strong like dollar fundamental data points

calls.condition: Score stays bearish if NFP comes in strong again.
calls.reason: Data scorecard GDP (-1), PCE (+1), ADP (-1) nets bearish for metals despite cooler PCE.
calls.quote: the outcome is still net bearish despite that cooler PCE print

notes: Transcript appears to be a clip; it does not discuss the dollar breakout named in the title explicitly beyond 'strong dollar fundamental data points'. DXY bias is implied (low conviction). Host already shorting Russell on some accounts; entry/stop not given. Russell target 2600 assumed to be in index points. No date spoken; GDP, PCE and ADP all described as out the same day.
